content: <thought>The mass spectrum shows a dominant peak at m/z 121.05 with an M+1 intensity of ~8 %, which is consistent with a compound containing about eight carbons (C₈). The ¹H NMR displays only aromatic signals: 2 H (dddd) at 7.47 ppm and 3 H (tt) at 7.64 ppm, totaling five aromatic protons typical of a monosubstituted benzene ring and no aliphatic protons. This pattern fits a phenyl ring bearing a substituent that has no hydrogens (e.g., a carbonyl directly attached to the ring). The most plausible formula that matches the observed mass and contains a carbonyl with no extra protons is C₈H₈O (acetophenone, C₆H₅‑CO‑CH₃). The M+1 peak (121 Da) arises from the natural ¹³C isotopic contribution of the eight carbons. Therefore, the SMILES for acetophenone is **CC(=O)c1ccccc1**.
